## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: driving under the influence and license suspensions and revocations
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical handbook page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The DUI page says an under-twenty-one driver at the lower alcohol level has the privilege suspended, while the penalty page lists the same case as a revocation for a set number of days; the dossier uses neutral loss-of-privilege wording for the first page and the penalty page's own revocation wording only where it cites that page (verify NV-DUIS-D-UNDER21) [A01].
The young-driver page likewise says suspended for juvenile-court findings and then refers to the same revocation period; this is held under the same debt [A03].
The penalty page refers to a chapter number for the SR-22 that does not match the chapter where the handbook explains it; the cross-reference was not copied [A02].
Crash statistics on these pages come from different past years and sources; they are taught only as historical figures in C2.
Fines, jail ranges and the DUI school cost are taught exactly as printed and isolated as dynamic.

corpus_stability.reason: The Nevada Driver's Handbook carries one edition line on its cover (DMV 700 March 2024) and one copyright year on its title page, with a short key-changes list; nothing in the selected pages suggests more than one rewrite per year. The edition is about two and a half years old at intake, so currency is held as freshness debt in part A.

verification_debt.claim_text: The Nevada Driver's Handbook (DMV 700 March 2024) calls the under-21 .02% alcohol case a suspension on physical page 79 but lists it as a 185-day revocation on physical page 80, and calls the under-18 juvenile-court DUI finding a 185-day suspension on physical page 81 while referring to the same 185-day revocation period; the dossier follows each cited page's wording or uses neutral loss-of-privilege wording; confirm the correct legal term with the Nevada DMV or NRS.
